recall_prompt: Say how you would find the term independent of x — the power of x in the general term, the r that makes it zero, and the value of that term.
insider_note: The square root halves the power: x carries (10 − r)/2 − 2r, and that whole expression is set to zero. Treating √(x/3) as power 1 gives a wrong r before any arithmetic starts.

steps.label: General term and the power of x
steps.margin_note: First mark. √(x/3) = (x/3) to the power 1/2, so the power of x is (10 − r)/2 − 2r. Set it to zero.
steps.memory_tip: The square root halves the power, so x carries (10 − r)/2 − 2r. Set that whole expression to zero.
lines: For the term independent of x:

recall.must_convey: That the power of x in the general term is (10 − r)/2 − 2r, and setting it to zero gives r = 2.
accept: the power of x is ten minus r by two minus two r, set it to zero, ten minus r is four r, r is two

steps.why: A term independent of x is a term where the powers of x cancel exactly; the half-power from the root is why the equation has a fraction.
common_mistakes: Treating √(x/3) as having power 1 instead of 1/2.
Writing the power of x as 10 − r − 2r.
